name: Sports trivia (hard)
description: 50 hard questions about rules, famous athletes, events and records that no longer change. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: By how many centimetres did Bob Beamon's 8.90 m jump at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics beat the previous long jump world record?
items.explain: Beamon's leap beat the old mark by 55 cm, a huge margin in a record that had typically moved only a few centimetres at a time.

items.question: Whose 1991 jump finally surpassed Bob Beamon's long jump world record after it had stood for 23 years?
items.explain: Mike Powell of the United States jumped 8.95 m in 1991 to beat Beamon's 8.90 m.

items.question: In which Pennsylvania town did Wilt Chamberlain score 100 points for the Philadelphia Warriors in 1962?
items.explain: The Warriors played some "home" games in Hershey, and Chamberlain's 100-point game against the Knicks was played there on March 2, 1962.

items.question: In his 100-point game, Wilt Chamberlain made how many of his 32 free-throw attempts?
items.explain: Chamberlain made 28 of 32 free throws, a notable result for a player known as a poor free-throw shooter.

source.title: Wilt Chamberlain Scores 100 Points in One Game | EBSCO

items.question: What was Wilt Chamberlain's per-game scoring average in the 1961-62 NBA season, the year of his 100-point game?
items.explain: Chamberlain averaged 50.4 points per game in 1961-62, breaking his own record of 38.4 from the season before.

items.question: Which Warriors publicist scribbled "100" on a sheet of paper for Chamberlain to hold up for the famous post-game photo?
items.explain: PR man Harvey Pollack wrote "100" on a piece of paper in the locker room, producing one of sport's most iconic photographs.

items.question: Who was the catcher on the receiving end of Don Larsen's perfect game in the 1956 World Series?
items.explain: Yogi Berra caught the game and famously leapt into Larsen's arms after the final out; his mitt is held by the Baseball Hall of Fame.

source.title: Don Larsen defined World Series perfection | Baseball Hall of Fame

items.question: Which Brooklyn Dodgers batter struck out on a 1-2 pitch to complete Don Larsen's perfect game?
items.explain: Dale Mitchell was the 27th batter Larsen retired, ending the game with a called strikeout.

source.title: Don Larsen pitches only World Series perfect game | HISTORY

items.question: How many pitches did Don Larsen throw in his 1956 World Series perfect game?
items.explain: Larsen needed only 97 pitches to retire all 27 Dodgers batters.

source.title: Don Larsen defined World Series perfection | Baseball Hall of Fame

items.question: Which Dodgers pitcher took the loss opposite Don Larsen in Game 5 of the 1956 World Series?
items.explain: Sal Maglie pitched well, allowing five hits, but the Yankees won 2-0 behind Larsen's perfect game.

items.question: Which English leg-spinner bowled Don Bradman for a duck in his final Test innings in 1948?
items.explain: Eric Hollies bowled Bradman with a googly at The Oval, leaving his Test average at 99.94.

source.title: Sir Don Bradman: Bio, 99.94 Average, Records & Legacy | Cricscope

items.question: How many runs did Don Bradman need in his last Test innings to finish with a career average of exactly 100?
items.explain: Bradman needed just four runs but was dismissed for nought, finishing on 99.94.

items.question: At which English ground did Don Bradman play his final Test innings in 1948?
items.explain: His famous duck came at The Oval in 1948, in what turned out to be his last Test innings.

items.question: On which apparatus did Nadia Comăneci score the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics history?
items.explain: Her first 10 came on the uneven bars on 18 July 1976 in Montreal.

items.question: What score did the Montreal 1976 scoreboard display for Comăneci's first perfect 10, because it could show only three digits?
items.explain: The scoreboard had been built on the assumption that a 10 was impossible, so it showed 1.00.

items.question: How many perfect scores of 10.0 did Nadia Comăneci earn at the 1976 Montreal Olympics?
items.explain: She received seven perfect 10s in Montreal, on the way to three gold medals.

items.question: Which company, the Olympic timekeeper, built the electronic scoreboard that could not display a 10.00 in Montreal in 1976?
items.explain: Omega asked the IOC how many digits to allow and was told three would be enough, since a 10.00 was thought impossible.

items.question: Which Czechoslovak gymnast was first to score perfect 10s at a major post-1952 competition, at the 1967 European Championships?
items.explain: Čáslavská earned two perfect 10s at the 1967 European Championships, nine years before Comăneci's Olympic 10.

items.question: From which royal residence did the 1908 London Olympic marathon start, helping to fix the race at 26 miles 385 yards?
items.explain: The race ran from Windsor Castle to the stadium at White City, and the finish in front of the royal box produced the odd distance.

items.question: Roughly how long was the marathon at the first modern Olympics in Athens in 1896?
items.explain: The 1896 race was based on the legendary run from Marathon to Athens of about 40 km (25 miles). The 42.195 km standard came later.

items.question: In which year was the marathon added to the women's Olympic programme?
items.explain: The women's Olympic marathon debuted at the 1984 Games.

items.question: What was Roger Bannister's time when he ran the first sub-four-minute mile at Oxford in 1954?
items.explain: Bannister ran 3 minutes 59.4 seconds at Iffley Road on 6 May 1954. The previous record was 4:01.4.

source.title: Sub-four minute mile plaque | Oxfordshire Blue Plaques Board

items.question: Which two friends paced Roger Bannister in his 1954 sub-four-minute mile?
items.explain: Chris Chataway and Chris Brasher set the pace for Bannister at the Iffley Road track.

source.title: Sub-four minute mile plaque | Oxfordshire Blue Plaques Board

items.question: Which Australian runner bettered Bannister's mile record the following month, in June 1954?
items.explain: John Landy ran 3:57.9 weeks after Bannister's run, and later lost to him in the "Miracle Mile" at the Empire Games.

source.title: Roger Bannister: First sub-four-minute mile | Guinness World Records

items.question: How many players made up each team in the first basketball game, played in 1891?
items.explain: Eighteen students were split into two teams of nine for James Naismith's first game.

items.question: At which university did James Naismith become the first men's basketball coach, serving from 1898 to 1907?
items.explain: Naismith coached the Kansas Jayhawks from 1898 to 1907 and became the program's first coach.

items.question: In Naismith's original game, what restarted play after each made basket?
answers: An inbound pass by the other team
items.explain: Because the baskets had no openings, a jump ball was held after every made basket.

items.question: Joe DiMaggio's 56-game hitting streak passed the previous record, set in the 1890s by which player?
items.explain: DiMaggio broke Willie Keeler's long-standing record of 44 or 45 straight games with a hit.

source.title: DiMaggio breaks Keeler's mark | Baseball Hall of Fame

items.question: Which Cleveland Indians third baseman made two fine plays to rob DiMaggio of hits on the day his streak ended in 1941?
items.explain: Ken Keltner twice robbed DiMaggio on July 17, 1941, and the streak ended at 56 games.

items.question: What was Joe DiMaggio's batting average during his 56-game hitting streak?
items.explain: DiMaggio hit .408 during the streak, with 15 home runs and 55 RBI, and struck out only seven times.

source.title: DiMaggio singles to start hitting streak | Baseball Hall of Fame

items.question: Who rode Secretariat to his 31-length win in the 1973 Belmont Stakes?
items.explain: Ron Turcotte was Secretariat's jockey for the 1973 Triple Crown.

items.question: Which horse had been the previous Triple Crown winner before Secretariat's sweep in 1973?
items.explain: Citation won the Triple Crown in 1948, so Secretariat was the first winner in 25 years.

source.title: Secretariat named 35th-greatest athlete of the century | ESPN

items.question: Which rival, ridden by Laffit Pincay Jr., finished last in Secretariat's 1973 Belmont Stakes?
items.explain: Sham, the second favourite, suffered a leg injury and finished last, more than 45 lengths behind Secretariat.

source.title: Rivals Had a Different View of Secretariat's Belmont | BloodHorse

items.question: What prompted Abebe Bikila to run the 1960 Olympic marathon in Rome barefoot?
answers: His sponsor's shoes were lost in transit
Shoes he bought in Rome gave him blisters
A religious vow made before the Games
items.correct: Shoes he bought in Rome gave him blisters
items.explain: The shoes Bikila bought in Rome did not fit and caused blisters, so he ran barefoot as he had in training.

items.question: Which Moroccan runner took silver behind barefoot Abebe Bikila in the 1960 Olympic marathon?
items.explain: Rhadi Ben Abdesselam ran with Bikila at a blazing pace for the first 20 km and took silver.

items.question: Abebe Bikila was born on the same day as which Olympic event?
items.explain: Bikila was born on August 7, 1932, the day of the Los Angeles Olympic marathon.

items.question: Which British favourite did Emil Zátopek famously ask whether the pace was too fast during the 1952 Olympic marathon?
items.explain: Zátopek asked Jim Peters about the pace, was told it was not fast enough, then accelerated into the lead and won.

source.title: Athletics at the 1952 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon | Wikipedia

items.question: Which Frenchman won silver behind Emil Zátopek in both the 5,000 m and 10,000 m at the 1952 Olympics?
items.explain: Alain Mimoun of France was second to Zátopek in both track finals in Helsinki.

source.title: Athletics at the 1952 Summer Olympics | Wikipedia

items.question: On the afternoon Emil Zátopek won the 5,000 m in 1952, his wife Dana won Olympic gold in which event?
items.explain: Dana Zátopková won the javelin the same afternoon, giving the couple two golds in one day.

items.question: Pelé scored his first World Cup goal in the 1958 quarter-final against which team?
items.explain: Pelé scored the only goal against Wales, making him the youngest goalscorer in World Cup history.

source.title: World Cup's Greatest Goals: Pele (1958, Brazil vs. Sweden) | ESPN

items.question: Who scored a record 13 goals at the 1958 World Cup in Sweden?
items.explain: Just Fontaine of France was the top scorer at the 1958 World Cup with 13 goals.

items.question: In which years did Pelé win his three men's World Cups?
items.explain: Pelé won the World Cup with Brazil in 1958, 1962 and 1970, and remains the only player to win three.

items.question: The 1958 World Cup produced the tournament's first 0-0 match, played between which two teams?
items.explain: The goalless draw between Brazil and England was the first 0-0 in World Cup finals history.

source.title: Football World Cup 1958 in Sweden | FootballHistory.org

items.question: What distance, an Olympic record, did Jesse Owens jump to win the long jump gold in Berlin in 1936?
items.explain: Owens won with an Olympic record 8.06 m on his sixth jump, ahead of Luz Long's 7.87 m.

source.title: Historic 1936 Olympic medal won by Jesse Owens friend Carl "Luz" Long up for bid | Sports Collectors Digest

items.question: Which German long jumper advised Jesse Owens on his run-up after two fouls in qualifying, then took silver?
items.explain: Luz Long suggested Owens mark a take-off point behind the board. Owens qualified and won gold, with Long second.

source.title: Luz Long's silver medal from 1936 Berlin Olympics long jump duel with Jesse Owens | CBS Sports

items.question: The 4x100 m relay team that Jesse Owens joined in 1936 set a world record that stood for how long?
items.explain: Owens was a late addition to the US relay team, which set a world record that stood for 20 years.

source.title: Jesse Owens | U.S. Olympic & Paralympic Museum

items.question: Who did Rod Laver beat in the 1969 US Open final to complete his second calendar-year Grand Slam?
items.explain: Laver beat fellow Australian Tony Roche 7-9, 6-1, 6-2, 6-2 to win all four majors in 1969.

source.title: September 9, 1969: The day Laver won the calendar Grand Slam again | Tennis Majors

items.question: Who, in 1938, became the first man to win all four major singles titles in a single year, before Rod Laver did so?
items.explain: Don Budge won the Grand Slam in 1938. Laver was the second man to do it (1962) and the first to repeat it (1969).

items.question: In which year did Rod Laver win his first calendar-year Grand Slam, as an amateur?
items.explain: Laver won all four majors in 1962 as an amateur and repeated the feat in 1969 as a professional.

source.title: September 9, 1969: The day Laver won the calendar Grand Slam again | Tennis Majors

items.question: How many Grand Slam singles titles did Rod Laver win in his career?
items.explain: Laver won 11 Grand Slam singles titles, plus six in men's doubles and three in mixed doubles.

source.title: August 9, 1938: The day Rod Laver was born | Tennis Majors
